I really enjoyed Resident Evil 3 Remake. The gameplay was fast, smooth, and fun, and I especially liked the dodge mechanic and the encounters with Nemesis. The atmosphere was great, and Jill and Carlos were both enjoyable characters.
I finished the game on Normal difficulty, but honestly, I found it a little too easy. My biggest issue was the length, as I wished there was more exploration and more content.
Overall, it was a really fun experience, and I’d give it an 8/10.

This is a short but sweet game. Unlike other RE fans I haven't played the original, so I have nothing to compare it to, but for what it is, I enjoyed it. The addition of a evade button benefited the game greatly, as zombies can get really annoying fast in these Resident Evil games and overall the level design felt tighter and more cohesive than Resident Evil 2.

I deeply enjoyed Nemesis and how comitted it is to hunting down Jill, even though he doesn't have the same stalker qualities of Mister X. Jill is also an interesting character and I deeply enjoyed the character of Carlos, however brief it may be.

While it doesn't soar to the heights of RE4 after it, for what it is (a short action packed movie like game), I think it gets the job done. I recommend it.

Resident Evil 3 is a solid survival horror game that delivers a tense and action-focused experience in the Resident Evil universe. It keeps the core elements of the series while leaning more into faster-paced gameplay compared to earlier entries.

The gameplay is smooth and responsive, with satisfying combat and a dodge mechanic that adds some depth to encounters. Managing resources still matters, which helps keep some tension even during more action-heavy moments.

Nemesis is one of the standout parts of the game. Being chased by him creates pressure and unpredictability, especially when he appears unexpectedly during exploration.

The atmosphere and setting do a good job of showing the chaos of Raccoon City during the outbreak. It feels intense and fast-moving, though it doesn’t always reach the same level of horror as other entries in the series.

Overall, Resident Evil 3 is an enjoyable but fairly short entry in the series. It has strong moments and fun gameplay, but its shorter length and lighter horror focus hold it back a bit. 

Gameplay: 7/10 Good | Overall: 7/10 Good

I'm gonna compare this game to RE2 Remake a lot. All of us know that RE3 was riding the gravy train of RE2's success, so CAPCOM apparently didn't put as much effort into this game as they did with RE2.

I haven't played the original, but this game isn't bad at all, it's way too overhated by those geeky purists who keep comparing it to the original. Was the game "short"? Not really. I'd say it's almost the same length as RE2. You could definitely finish it in one sitting. Was this game beautiful enough to make you cream a bit? Most definitely, especially with RTX on. And don't get me started with the RE Engine. I've never seen such a stable and flat frame graph in my life with FPS reaching the sky. CAPCOM killed it with the graphics, optimization and the engine.

With that being said, this game is the polar opposite of RE2. This game is wayyy more action oriented, while RE2 was more horror/terror oriented. You could go nuking the whole city with an RPG with no fear of Nemesis sneaking up to you. It's a complete psychological overhaul where there's no consequences of walking too fast/loudly, shooting guns that creates noise etc. So coming from RE2, I had to completely change my playstyle.

At first I thought the dodge mechanic would be a saving grace as that didn't exist in RE2 but ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ is it hard to perfect it. 9/10 times you'll just dodge too early or too late, heck, maybe dodge TOWARDS the enemy who's trying to kill you.

Here's a nitpick about RE games in general: the pointless habit of doing headshots. Logically you'd think one headshot would be fatal and kill those ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ instantly, but nahhhhh, sometimes you'd be shooting 10 bullets and they still won't die, so ♥♥♥♥ THAT.

My boi Carlos is the comic relief of the entire game. He's just a likeable dude yk? He'd make those cheesy yet funny Leon oneliners, make random remarks about random things, and playing as him with his assault rifle really sealed the deal for me.

Last but not …

claims.claim: Reviewers report that the game is very short, with story playthroughs lasting only a few hours.

citations.review_text:
Capcom looked at the massive success and critical praise of RE2 Remake, then assigned RE3 to a junior team and told them to ship it in half the time with a quarter of the budget. The result is a game that looks pretty, runs fine, and feels like a DLC that somehow cost $60.

The core problem is simple: it's absurdly short. We're talking 3-5 hours for a story mode that feels incomplete because it literally is. Major locations from the original — the clock tower, the cemetery, the factory — are just gone. Nemesis, the game's supposedly terrifying pursuer, is a neutered liability compared to Mr. X from RE2. He shows up, you dodge him (a new mechanic that trivializes him), and he leaves. The tension evaporates. The game feels rushed because it was rushed, outsourced to work around RE8's development schedule, and it shows in every compromised design decision.

You can see where cuts were made — not artistic choices, but genuine missing content. The Mercenaries mode that was in RE2 isn't here. The polish is there, the visuals are sharp, but it's a feature-complete game squeezed into the skeleton of a proper remake. Playing RE2 Remake first makes RE3 feel insulting: you get the sense Capcom figured out how to make these work, then intentionally shaved off 70% of the experience because shipping faster was more important than respecting players' time and money.

It's not bad — it's cynically incomplete. For $60, that's a thumbs down.

Play RE2 Remake instead, or honestly wait for RE4's price to drop. Neither will leave you feeling robbed.

The game was really great, but it had a rather short story. Even without focusing on collecting all the secondary items, you can finish the game in about 1 hour to 1 hour and 20 minutes. This is because the remake has removed many sections compared to the original version.

Removed content compared to the original:
The Clock Tower area (which was a major location in the original)
The Park and Cemetery sections
The Worm enemies (Grave Digger)
The live-choice system that affected story branches
Some puzzles and exploration segments
The Mercenaries mode (replaced with Resistance mode)
Certain boss fight phases and alternate routes

My suggestion:
I definitely recommend buying this game — I personally purchased it during a sale, and I think it's worth it at a discounted price.

Absolute peak game (at least for me :>), would definitely recommend, this is also a pretty nice start to the re franchise...the only thing i dont like about this game is the length of the game and missing scenes from the og re3, i wouldve loved it a lot if i could get more gameplay, capcom shouldnt really have rushed it then it might have been better...but still nice, even the character designs/faces, voice of the characters, and the voice lines are so damn good :)..

It takes no time to finish the game.
About five hours if I remember correctly.
Had all the achievments in about twenty hours.
The actual gameplay is pretty fun and Jill is an actual badass.
Get it but get it on sale.

This is my first resident evil experience of actually playing the games in this franchise. I am aware that this game is considered an incomplete remake of the original and from what I've seen I'd agree with that statement. However I purchased this game on a 90% sale and for that price? I'd say every penny was worth it. Would I purchase it for it's full price? Most likely not. But it would be doing a great disservice to this game by saying that it is not fun. It's length is often brought up as it's major downside but for someone only getting into the franchise (playing the games) I'd say it's actually a good thing. That way it doesn't overwhelm you with a ton of puzzles to solve (there aren't any real puzzles in this remake) or too many areas to explore or backtrack to. With that said I do think that there could've been more to it and it's a shame there isn't. That doesn't stop the game from being an extreme blast though. I love the fact that this game leans more into action with Carlos' sections and Jill's dodge ability makes her encounters even more engaging than just looping around an object or running away. It also adds more skill in the sense of timing your dodges rather than just knowing the game in and out (You'll quickly learn everything there is to it though because it's so short). The difficulties in my opinion are some of the best I've played through. Nightmare difficulty brings with it completely different enemy spawns while also making them more aggressive and not just bullet sponges (though they still do take more hits to take down, which I am not a huge fan of). Items have also different locations which does change how you route your approach, which adds extra replayability to an otherwise short experience. You can very quickly finish the challenges that require multiple playthroughs (or just one if you're doing them all in one go) that is really good when you're trying to complete all that there is to the game. Except maybe the "kill X enemies using Y…

Overall it's a fun and thrilling RE game, i recomend it if you're new to the Resident Evil franchise cause its has short play time. but the story is too short. literally you can speedrun this game like super fast, too bad capcom cut significant amount of it's content from RE3 Original.

This game is okay in its own right if you don't compare it to the original Resident Evil 3. It's replayable and enjoyable, but it's very scripted, and it's very easy to cheese the game, which makes it feel a bit like a farce.

The fact that you can farm zombies at one point in the game to unlock the infinite rocket launcher makes each playthrough feel less about skill and more about how well you know the game's scripted layout.

With some of the extras unlocked, the game can easily be completed in under an hour.

Unfortunately, large sections from the original seem to have been cut, including Raccoon Park, the Graveyard, the Dead Factory, and many of the Downtown streets. The gas station and the clock tower are vivid memories for me, and here they're reduced to little more than footnotes.

All in all, I'd give it a 6/10. I'd play it, but don't compare it to the original.

After completing the game on every difficulty, earning every achievement, and finishing Inferno with an S Rank, I can confidently say that Resident Evil 3 Remake is a very good game that suffers more from expectations than from its actual quality.

Coming directly from Resident Evil 2 Remake, the first thing I noticed was how much more linear this game is. RE2 feels like a giant interconnected puzzle box where exploration, route planning, and resource management are constantly rewarded. RE3 is much more focused on momentum, action, and pushing the player forward.

This difference explains a lot of the criticism the game received.

After learning more about the original Resident Evil 3, I understand why longtime fans were disappointed. Entire areas such as the Clock Tower and the Park were removed, which likely contributed to the shorter length and more linear structure. However, since I never played the original, I judged this remake on its own merits rather than comparing it to a game I had never experienced.

And on its own merits, it's a lot of fun.

Jill is fantastic to play. The dodge mechanic adds a layer of skill expression that rewards timing and practice, especially on higher difficulties. Inferno difficulty in particular transforms the game into a genuine challenge and gives the combat system a chance to shine.

Nemesis is also a great antagonist, although I personally preferred Mr. X from Resident Evil 2 Remake. Mr. X created constant strategic pressure while allowing more exploration. Nemesis is more aggressive and action-oriented, but combined with the game's linear design, he often pushes the pace forward instead of creating long-term tension.

Carlos was another pleasant surprise. I enjoyed his sections, even if they felt a little short. His personality and gameplay helped break up the campaign nicely.

My biggest criticism is simply that I wanted more of the game. Not because I wasn't enjoying it, but because I was. The campaign feels…

Overall it's a fun and thrilling RE game, i recomend it if you're new to the Resident Evil franchise cause its has short play time. but the story is too short. literally you can speedrun this game like super fast, too bad capcom cut significant amount of it's content from RE3 Original.

claims.claim: Reviewers note that the game leans much more heavily into fast-paced action rather than traditional survival horror.

citations.review_text: Coming straight from Resident Evil 2 Remake, Resident Evil 3 Remake feels like a breath of fresh air. Its faster-paced, more action-oriented gameplay is a welcome change from RE2's survival horror style, and playing as Jill Valentine is simply badass. The game is on the short side, so I'd recommend picking it up when it's on sale.

Very fun game, but a bit disappointing compared to both the original and Resident Evil 2 Remake.

Graphics are fantastic. The character models are incredibly detailed, the zombies look disgusting in the best possible way, and Raccoon City has never looked better. The streets, buildings, sewers, and hospital are all beautifully crafted and packed with detail. The animations are excellent, making movement and combat feel smooth and responsive. Jill and Carlos received excellent redesigns, and the overall presentation is top-notch. The only disappointment is that some iconic locations from the original game were either heavily reduced or completely removed.

Sound effects are great. The zombies, creatures, gunshots, explosions, and environmental sounds all help create a tense atmosphere. The soundtrack is good, although it feels less memorable than some previous entries in the franchise. The voice acting is excellent; the characters feel much more believable and natural than their original counterparts. The banter between Jill, Carlos, and the supporting cast helps make the story more enjoyable.

Gameplay is great and very fun. The combat feels more polished than Resident Evil 2 Remake, thanks to the addition of the dodge mechanic, which gives you more options when dealing with enemies. Weapons feel powerful, movement is fluid, and the overall pace is faster. The game leans much more heavily into action than survival horror, which is a bit disappointing, but the original made that shift too, so it is what it is.

Resource management still exists, but it is significantly less demanding than in previous games. Ammunition and healing items are generally plentiful if you explore, and the game often encourages aggressive play rather than careful conservation of resources. Exploration remains enjoyable, but the more linear structure means there is less backtracking, fewer puzzles, and less of that classic survival horror feeling.

The enemies are excellent. Zombies…

A great cinematic action experience with good amounts of survival horror elements. Plenty of replayability with multiple difficulties and a slew of unlockables. It's an RE engine game, so it looks and runs great. It's RE2R but more linear and with significantly improved action. 

This game has gotten a bad reputation from people with nostalgia or dated taste for the original game. The tank control games are fine, but fans froth at the mouth vehemently defending them to the point of putting minor pieces of content on a pedestal and denigrating technically and artistically great games like this one. Arguably, the game didn't have enough content for full price, which you could have said about the original as well, but being able to snag this for $3.99 on Steam makes it a steal.

Coming directly from Resident Evil 2 Remake, the first thing I noticed was how much more linear this game is. RE2 feels like a giant interconnected puzzle box where exploration, route planning, and resource management are constantly rewarded. RE3 is much more focused on momentum, action, and pushing the player forward.

This difference explains a lot of the criticism the game received.

Entire areas such as the Clock Tower and the Park were removed, which likely contributed to the shorter length and more linear structure. And on its own merits, it's a lot of fun.

I still highly recommend picking it up on a huge sale because the core gameplay/gunplay is a lot of fun. [h2]Nota Geral | Overall Rating[/h2]
⭐⭐⭐

[b]Resident Evil 3 Remake é um caso curioso: pega tudo que funcionou em RE2 Remake e aplica com a mesma qualidade técnica, mas erra feio em um ponto que deveria ser básico. A duração é ridícula, quase uma ofensa ao consumidor, e isso pesa demais em um pacote que, tecnicamente, é impecável. É difícil recomendar o jogo no preço cheio quando a sensação que fica é de ter jogado uma DLC cara disfarçada de jogo completo.[/b]

[i]Resident Evil 3 Remake is a curious case: it takes everything that worked in RE2 Remake and applies it with the same technical quality, but badly misses on something that should be basic. The length is ridiculous, almost an insult to the consumer, and that weighs too much on a package that is, technically, flawless. It's hard to recommend the game at full price when what's left is the feeling of having played an expensive DLC disguised as a complete game.[/i]

[h2]Jogabilidade | Gameplay[/h2]
⭐⭐⭐⭐⭐

[b]A jogabilidade é ótima porque segue a base sólida que RE2 Remake construiu, e isso não é demérito nenhum. Cada combate se torna uma decisão entre gastar munição, esquivar no timing certo ou simplesmente correr, e essa tensão constante é o que mantém o combate interessante do início ao fim.[/b]

[i]The gameplay is great because it follows the solid foundation RE2 Remake built, and that's no demerit at all. Very fun game, but a bit disappointing compared to both the original and Resident Evil 2 Remake.

Graphics are fantastic. The character models are incredibly detailed, the zombies look disgusting in the best possible way, and Raccoon City has never looked better. The streets, buildings, sewers, and hospital are all beautifully crafted and packed with detail. The animations are excellent, making movement and combat feel smooth and responsive. Jill and Carlos received excellent redesigns, and the overall presentation is top-notch. The only disappointment is that some iconic locations from the original game were either heavily reduced or completely removed.

Sound effects are great. The zombies, creatures, gunshots, explosions, and environmental sounds all help create a tense atmosphere. The soundtrack is good, although it feels less memorable than some previous entries in the franchise. The voice acting is excellent; the characters feel much more believable and natural than their original counterparts. The banter between Jill, Carlos, and the supporting cast helps make the story more enjoyable.

Gameplay is great and very fun. The combat feels more polished than Resident Evil 2 Remake, thanks to the addition of the dodge mechanic, which gives you more options when dealing with enemies. Weapons feel powerful, movement is fluid, and the overall pace is faster. The game leans much more heavily into action than survival horror, which is a bit disappointing, but the original made that shift too, so it is what it is.

Resource management still exists, but it is significantly less demanding than in previous games. Ammunition and healing items are generally plentiful if you explore, and the game often encourages aggressive play rather than careful conservation of resources. Exploration remains enjoyable, but the more linear structure means there is less backtracking, fewer puzzles, and less of that classic survival horror feeling.
